To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

evolutionary learning of topologically flexible network architectures under the constraint of implementing elementary computational steady-state functions produces robust networks, capable of multiplexer and transfer learning.

evolutionary learning of networks under the constraint to implement a steady-state input-output operation produces large controllable networks, which can multiplex different computations, and exhibit transfer learning.

evolutionary learning of topologically flexible neural network circuits, constrained to compute elementary steady-state input-output computations, results in robust, large circuits capable of multiplexed computations, and transfer learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental question of how to learn and control large networks, with a particular focus on the biological context.
the question how the structure and function of a network can evolve and how the network can be controlled.
the fundamental problem of how to learn a network that computes a steady-state function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework is a new and general approach for the discovery of topologically flexible, controllable, multiplexable, and transferable networks for computation of steady-state functions.

the proposed evolutionary learning method of networks is capable of producing controllable, multiplexable, and transfer learning circuits, which could serve as a basis for biologically inspired computations.
the proposed framework provides a new perspective on learning in networks, and opens up the field to a wide variety of new research directions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new framework for evolutionary learning of networks implementing steady state input-output operations.
we introduce a framework for evolutionary learning of networks, and show that the learned networks have remarkable properties of controllability, multiplexing, and transfer learning.
the proposed framework provides a general and flexible method for the discovery of network based computations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
evolutionary learning of networks can be used as a design principle for constructing controllable, multiplexed, and transfer learning capable networks.
the evolutionary search and learning method can identify networks implementing steady-state functions, and that such networks are controllable and robust, and can multiplex and transfer learn.
the evolutionary search and learning framework can produce robust and flexible networks that are capable of learning multiple steady-state input-output computations.
